messages.content: What is Mycelium?

Mycelium is a P2P on-device AI app that runs language models directly on your phone using Metal GPU acceleration. No cloud, no API keys, no data leaves your device. It uses lightweight LoRA adapters that propagate peer-to-peer through the Spore network, giving you regionally relevant knowledge without centralized servers.
What is the Spore protocol?

Spore is a peer-to-peer social protocol where short-form posts called 'spores' propagate directly between devices without centralized content servers. It uses a minimal control plane inspired by Tailscale's architecture, with all content flowing device-to-device via encrypted QUIC tunnels. The network is the mycelium — users produce spores that spread organically through geographic gossip.
How does Mycelium work?

Mycelium works in a few steps: 1) Download a base language model (~1GB) on first launch. 2) All inference runs locally on your phone's GPU. 3) When you ask a question, the app extracts topic tags and searches the P2P network for relevant LoRA adapters. 4) Matching adapters download automatically and activate for your question. 5) You get specialized answers enhanced by community knowledge — all on-device.
What is a LoRA adapter?

A LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) adapter is a small file (10-50MB) that specializes a base AI model for a particular topic or domain. Instead of retraining the entire model, LoRA adjusts a small number of weight matrices. Multiple adapters can stack simultaneously — so you can have slang + food + news LoRAs all active at once, combining their knowledge.
Is my data private on Mycelium?

Yes, completely. All AI processing happens on your device. Your conversations never leave your phone — there's no cloud processing, no API calls to external services, and no server storing your chat history. Only the weight deltas (adapters) propagate through the network, not your personal data or conversations.
How do LoRA adapters spread through the network?

LoRA adapters propagate through geographic gossip over the Spore protocol. When you connect to the network, your device discovers available adapters from nearby peers and a coordination bot. Adapters are matched to your questions by tags — if you ask about local food, adapters tagged 'food' + your city will be found and downloaded. Peers can also serve adapters directly to each other via local network discovery (mDNS).
What model does Mycelium use?

On iPhone, Mycelium offers model selection based on your device's RAM: SmolLM2 360M for basic devices, SmolLM2 1.7B for most iPhones (the recommended default), and Llama 3.2 3B for Pro models with 8GB RAM. On Mac, it defaults to Llama 3.1 8B for best quality. All models are quantized to Q4_K_M format for efficiency.
How is Spore different from Twitter?

Spore has no central server holding your data. Posts propagate peer-to-peer through geographic gossip — like real conversation spreading through a neighborhood. There's no algorithm deciding what you see, no company that can ban you or sell your data. Your identity is a cryptographic key, posts are immutable (no deletes), and verified users earn amplification by proving they're human, not by paying.
Can I train my own LoRA adapter?

Yes! On the Mac version of Mycelium, you can train custom LoRA adapters from RSS feeds, text files, or pasted content. The app handles everything — content analysis, Q&A pair generation, MLX-based training, and GGUF conversion. You can then share your adapter to the Spore network for others to use. Training is Mac-only because it needs more compute than a phone provides.
What is DERP in Spore?

DERP is the relay fallback for when direct peer-to-peer connections can't be established (about 8% of connections, usually behind symmetric NAT). It forwards encrypted blobs between peers — it cannot decrypt the content. Think of it as a safety net postal service: it delivers sealed envelopes without reading them. Direct QUIC connections are always preferred.
How does Spore handle spam?

Spore uses a reputation-based moderation system. Anonymous peers cannot relay content (limiting spam blast radius). Verified peers get higher reach. Users can report content, and the reputation oracle aggregates reports weighted by the reporter's own score. At threshold, content stops propagating. Additionally, posts have TTL (time-to-live) hops that limit how far they travel based on the author's verification tier.
What encryption does Spore use?

Spore uses Ed25519 for identity keypairs and signatures, X25519 for key exchange, XChaCha20-Poly1305 for symmetric encryption, and BLAKE2b for hashing. All peer connections are encrypted via QUIC (TLS 1.3). Direct messages use X25519 key exchange with AES-256-GCM, providing end-to-end encryption that not even relay nodes can break.
How do I back up my Spore identity?

Your Spore identity can be backed up as a BIP39 mnemonic — 24 words that encode your private key. Write these down and store them safely. If you lose your device, you can restore your identity on a new device from the mnemonic. There's no server-side key escrow — lost mnemonic means lost identity forever. No 'forgot password' flow exists by design.
What does 'verified' mean on Spore?

Verification on Spore (Spore+) proves you're a unique human without revealing your identity. Currently it uses web-of-trust: 3+ existing Spore+ users vouch for you. Verified users get higher TTL (their posts travel further), can relay others' content across geographic boundaries, and earn a verified badge. It's an earned status that gives you amplification, not a purchased checkmark.
How does geographic gossip work?

Peers are organized into geographic buckets (geohash prefix, ~city-level). When you post, your spore pushes to your inner ring (8 peers in same city), outer ring (4 peers in adjacent areas), and any follow-targets. Verified peers re-gossip to their neighbors, amplifying content. The radius adapts: sparse areas use wide radius (hundreds of km) so feeds don't feel empty, while dense cities narrow to neighborhoods.
Does Mycelium work offline?

Yes. Once the base model and adapters are downloaded, everything runs locally — even in airplane mode. You only need internet to discover and download new adapters. The AI inference is completely on-device using your phone's Metal GPU. You can chat with the AI anywhere, anytime, with whatever adapters you already have installed.
What's the Substrate in Spore?

The Substrate is Spore's minimal control plane. It handles STUN/TURN for NAT traversal, peer registration with approximate geographic location, handle resolution (looking up pubkeys by username), and reputation scoring. Critically, it does NOT know what anyone posts, who follows whom, or any message content. It only facilitates peer discovery — all content flows peer-to-peer.
How are DMs handled in Spore?

DMs in Spore are end-to-end encrypted using X25519 key exchange + AES-256-GCM. They're delivered directly if the recipient is online, via DERP relay if they're on the network but not directly reachable, or stored temporarily by the bot (encrypted, TTL 7 days) for offline delivery. No server or relay can read the content — only the recipient's private key can decrypt.
What platforms does Mycelium support?

Mycelium is available on iOS (iPhone and iPad, iOS 17+), macOS (Apple Silicon Macs, macOS 14+), and Android (arm64 devices, Android 9+). The iOS and macOS versions share the same codebase. The Mac version additionally supports LoRA training. All platforms connect to the same Spore network and share adapters cross-platform.
Why does Mycelium use small models instead of GPT-4?

Because a small model + many community LoRAs beats a big cloud model that knows nothing about your world. A 1.7B model with a local slang LoRA will answer 'what does hella mean?' better than GPT-4 which gives a generic dictionary definition. Plus: it's private (no data sent to OpenAI), free (no API costs), works offline, and the community knowledge compounds over time through P2P sharing.
How does the tag matching work for LoRAs?

When you ask a question, Mycelium uses the local model to extract 3-5 topic tags from your query (a quick 30-token inference). These tags are matched against the catalog of available LoRAs using accent-insensitive comparison. A LoRA needs at least 2 matching tags to be considered relevant. The top 2 matches are downloaded (if not already installed) and activated for your response.
What is the 'brain counter' in Mycelium?

The brain emoji counter (e.g., '2 🧠') in the top-left toolbar shows how many LoRA adapters are currently active in memory. Tapping it shows which specific adapters are influencing your AI's responses right now. The stack icon in the top-right opens the full library for managing all installed adapters.
Can Spore posts be deleted?

No. Spore posts are immutable — once published, they cannot be deleted from the network. This is by design: 'assholes live forever.' What you say stays said, just like real life. You can block users (hiding their content from your view) and report content (reducing their network reach), but there's no central authority that can retroactively erase posts.
How does Mycelium's text-to-speech work?

Mycelium has a TTS toggle (speaker icon in the toolbar). When enabled, the AI speaks its responses sentence-by-sentence as they generate — you hear the answer while text appears simultaneously. It uses iOS's built-in AVSpeechSynthesizer, works in any language your device supports, runs completely on-device, and the system prompt automatically shortens responses to keep them concise for listening.
What's a 'spore' in the network?

A spore is a single post on the Spore network — analogous to a tweet. It's a signed piece of text (max 512 bytes) that propagates through the peer-to-peer network. Each spore has an ID (BLAKE2b hash), author public key, timestamp, optional parent (for threading), the body text, and an Ed25519 signature proving authenticity.
How do I follow someone on Spore?

You resolve their handle through the Substrate (which returns their public key), then connect directly to their device (or their relay peers). A signed follow request is sent peer-to-peer. Their device begins pushing new spores to you. The Substrate never knows you follow them — it only facilitated the initial lookup. Your follow list is stored only on your device.
What is the Spore address format?

Spore addresses use bech32 encoding with a 'spore1' prefix, followed by the encoded Ed25519 public key. For example: spore1qw508d6qejxtdg4y5r3zarvaryvg6kdaj. This is your permanent identity on the network — derived from your private key, human-readable, and globally unique without any registration authority.
How does boosting work in Spore?

Boosting is Spore's decentralized retweet. When a verified peer boosts a spore, its TTL (time-to-live) is reset to the booster's tier value and re-gossipped as if new. This is human editorial judgment at the network layer — not an algorithm. Each peer can only boost a given spore once, and the original spore is unmodified. Anonymous peers can boost too, just with lower TTL.
What's the difference between the phone and Mac version of Mycelium?

The phone version is for inference only — chat with AI, download LoRAs from the network, and get answers enhanced by community knowledge. The Mac version adds training capabilities: you can create new LoRA adapters from RSS feeds, text files, or pasted content using MLX-based training, then share them to the Spore network. The Mac also uses a larger model (Llama 3.1 8B) for better quality.
How does Spore protect against surveillance?

Spore's threat model covers ISPs, governments, and corporations. All connections are QUIC-encrypted (looks like generic UDP). The Substrate never sees content or social graph. DMs are end-to-end encrypted. Follow lists are local-only. There's no central database to subpoena. The main weakness is a global passive adversary doing timing correlation — which would require Tor-level mix networking to defeat.
What happens when I ask a question in Mycelium?

Here's the full flow: 1) Your question goes to the local model for tag extraction (quick 30-token inference). 2) Tags are matched against the LoRA catalog (needs 2+ matches). 3) Top 2 uninstalled matches download via DERP chunked transfer (512KB chunks). 4) All current LoRAs deactivate, top 2 relevant ones activate. 5) The model generates a response with those adapters applied. 6) Attribution shows which LoRAs contributed.
Can I use Mycelium without connecting to the network?

Absolutely. The base model works standalone — you get a general-purpose AI assistant running entirely on your device. The network connection is only for discovering and downloading LoRA adapters to enhance it. You can disconnect anytime and keep chatting with whatever adapters you already have installed. The app functions fully offline.
What is the LoRA library in Mycelium?

The LoRA Library (accessible via the stack icon) shows all your installed adapters — their names, tags, source URLs, and active/inactive status. You can toggle adapters on/off, swipe to delete individual ones, or delete all for a fresh start. It also shows adapters available from nearby peers that you haven't installed yet.
How does peer discovery work in Mycelium?

Mycelium discovers peers two ways: 1) mDNS on your local network — devices advertising the _mycelium._udp service on port 9010 can serve LoRAs directly via QUIC. 2) The DERP relay connects you to the Spore bot which serves the catalog and LoRA binaries. Local peer transfer is always tried first, falling back to the bot for adapters not available nearby.
What is the quality gate for training LoRAs?

Before training starts, Mycelium checks: 1) Minimum ~1,000 tokens of content (roughly 3-4 pages). 2) At least 30 Q&A pairs can be generated. 3) Content isn't too repetitive (trigram diversity must be above 30%). If any check fails, you get a clear explanation and can go back to add more content. This prevents wasting training time on data that would produce a useless adapter.
How is Spore governed?

Currently it's a benevolent dictator model during early development. The protocol spec is CC-BY-SA 4.0 (open, forkable), and the implementation is MIT licensed. At v1.0, governance transitions to a community RFC process. Anyone can fork the protocol or run their own infrastructure — there's no lock-in to any single entity.
What's the Spore web gateway?

The web gateway at getspore.xyz is a read-only discovery layer — like a shop window for the network. It shows trending handles, profile info, and preview content from super-peers who opt in. It stores only metadata and pointers, never content permanently. If the gateway goes down, the network is completely unaffected. It exists for onboarding and discoverability only.
How does the daily news LoRA pipeline work?

Every day, the pipeline fetches RSS feeds from 11 news sources (NPR, PBS, AP News, Agência Brasil, and 7 Bay Area/California local papers). For each article, it generates 3 Q&A variations. These are formatted as chat JSONL and used to train a LoRA adapter using MLX (500 iterations, rank 8, all layers). The output is converted to GGUF format and published to the bot's catalog with geographic tags.
What devices can run Mycelium?

Any iPhone 12 or later (iOS 17+), any Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 14+), or any Android phone with arm64 CPU and 4GB+ RAM (Android 9+). The 360M model runs on anything, the 1.7B model needs 4GB+ free RAM, and the 3B model needs 6GB+. For training, you need a Mac — any M1 or later with 8GB+ unified memory works great.
What makes Mycelium different from ChatGPT?

Three fundamental differences: 1) Privacy — nothing leaves your device, ever. ChatGPT sends everything to OpenAI's servers. 2) Community knowledge — LoRAs from your local community make the model know things no cloud model knows (local slang, seasonal food, transit tips). 3) No cost — no subscription, no API fees, no rate limits. The tradeoff is a smaller model, but LoRAs bridge that gap for topics that matter to you.
How does Spore handle content moderation?

Spore uses decentralized moderation through reputation scoring. Users report content, weighted by the reporter's own score. At threshold (7+ unique reports), content stops propagating. The developer reviews reports within 24 hours. Users also have local controls: Block (hide all from a user) and Hide (remove individual posts). There's zero tolerance for CSAM, harassment, and hate speech — reported via safety@getspore.xyz.
What is the adaptive geo-radius?

Spore adapts its propagation radius based on local peer density to solve the 'empty room' problem. With fewer than 10 peers within 500km, everything propagates widely. As density increases (10-50 peers → 200km, 50-200 peers → 50km, 200+ → standard geohash rings), the radius tightens. This means early users still see a busy feed even with sparse peers, while dense cities get neighborhood-level granularity.
What's the attribution feature in Mycelium?

When LoRAs contribute to a response, Mycelium shows a '🍄 via Source Name' footer below the message. For news LoRAs, this includes the publisher name and a tappable link to the original source. There's also a disclaimer: 'This adapter was trained on content from [source]. Mycelium does not guarantee responses accurately represent the original publisher's content.' This credits sources and protects everyone legally.
How do I get started with Spore?

Download the Spore app from the App Store (iOS) or get the APK for Android. On first launch, a cryptographic keypair is generated on your device — that's your identity. Choose a handle, and you're connected to peers in your geographic area. You'll immediately see local posts without following anyone. To follow specific people, search their handle. Everything is encrypted and peer-to-peer from the start.
What is the Spore influence system?

Instead of follower counts, Spore uses an influence score that determines how far your posts travel. Your score grows with likes, boosts, and posts that spread. Cross a whole number and your reach extends — your TTL increases so posts travel more hops. It's like leveling up: the more value you provide to the network, the wider your voice carries. No vanity metrics, just real reach.
Is Spore open source?

Yes. The protocol spec is CC-BY-SA 4.0 and the implementation is MIT licensed. Anyone can audit the design, build their own client, run relay nodes, or fork the protocol. The code is on GitHub. There are no proprietary servers or secret algorithms — everything is transparent and verifiable.
How does Mycelium's streaming TTS work?

When TTS is enabled, Mycelium doesn't wait for the full response — it speaks sentence-by-sentence as they generate. Each time a sentence boundary is detected (period, exclamation, question mark followed by a space), that sentence is immediately queued for speech. AVSpeechSynthesizer plays them sequentially. Text appears on screen simultaneously. If you toggle TTS off mid-response, speech stops immediately.
What's the GGUF format?

GGUF (GPT-Generated Unified Format) is the binary format used by llama.cpp for storing model weights and LoRA adapters. It's a compact, memory-mappable format optimized for fast loading on consumer hardware. All Mycelium models and adapters use GGUF. LoRA adapters in GGUF are typically 10-50MB and contain only the weight deltas (differences from the base model).
How many LoRAs can be active at once?

Mycelium activates up to 2 LoRA adapters per query — the top 2 most relevant matches from the catalog. Before each new question, all previously active adapters are deactivated, and the best matches for the current question are activated. This dynamic swapping means the model adapts its knowledge to each specific question rather than loading everything at once.
What is QUIC and why does Spore use it?

QUIC is a multiplexed, encrypted transport protocol built on UDP. Spore uses it because: 1) It looks like generic UDP to network observers (DPI-resistant). 2) It supports multiplexed streams (gossip, DMs, and sync over one connection). 3) It has built-in encryption (TLS 1.3). 4) It supports 0-RTT reconnection. 5) It handles NAT traversal better than TCP. It's the same technology Tailscale uses.
